summary: Reimon Yuki (1902–1992) studied at the University of Tokyo (~1924–1927). A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, he served as professor at the University of Tokyo (~1949–1963), at Kyoto Women's University (~1963–1973), and held an emeritus professorship at Ryukoku University.
Reiner Wiehl (1929–2010) was a philosopher who taught John Taber. He held academic posts at the University of Hamburg (~1970–1977) and Heidelberg University (~1977–1997).
Reinhold Grünendahl is an Indologist who held posts at the Free University of Berlin (attested 1983) and the Göttingen State and University Library (attested 2008).
Reinhold Klotz (1807–1870) was a linguist who studied at Leipzig University (~1826–1830). He later served on the faculty at Leipzig University (~1832–1870), where he taught Friedrich Max Müller.

Reinhold Rost (1822–1896) studied at the University of Jena (~1842–1847). A scholar of Indology and linguistics, he held posts at The King's School Canterbury, St Augustine's College, the Royal Asiatic Society, and as Librarian at the India Office.

Renate Syed (b. 1953) is an Indologist who completed her doctorate at Ludwig Maximilian University of Munich (~1976–1982). She studied under doctoral supervisor Dieter Schlingloff and teachers Friedrich Wilhelm and Gritli von Mitterwallner.
Renda Zheng (b. 1944) is a scholar in Buddhist studies. Zheng studied under traditional teachers Kaizhi, Shengfa, and Kaitong.

René Gothóni (b. 1950) studied at the University of Helsinki (~1970–1982). Specializing in religious and Buddhist studies, he held a post at the University of Helsinki from ~1975 to 2014 and taught Ilkka Pyysiäinen.

Richard A. Hutch (b. 1945) studied at Gettysburg College, Yale Divinity School, and the University of Chicago. A religious studies scholar, he held posts at Southern Illinois University (~1974–1978) and the University of Queensland (~1978–2010).
Richard B. Martin (1937–2004) worked in Indology and Tibetology. He served at the University of Virginia as a professor (attested 1983–1991) and as South Asian bibliographer (attested 2003).
Richard Baker (b. 1936), a Buddhist studies figure, studied at Harvard University and under Shunryu Suzuki in 1971, whom he later succeeded. He taught Philip Whalen and Taigen Dan Leighton.
Richard Barron works in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under traditional teachers Kalu Rinpoche, Dezhung Rinpoche Kunga Tenpai Nyima, and the 3rd Jamgön Kongtrul.
Richard Bowring (b. 1947) works in Japanology and Buddhist studies. He was educated at Blundell's School (~1960–1965) and Downing College (~1965–1969).

Richard Carnac Temple (1850–1931) studied at Harrow School and Trinity Hall. Working in Indology and archaeology, he served in the Bengal and Indian Staff Corps, and was editor and proprietor of The Indian Antiquary.
Richard D. Mann works in Indology and religious studies. He earned his PhD at McMaster University under the supervision of Phyllis Granoff (attested 2003).

Richard D. McBride II works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and history. He completed graduate studies at UCLA with mentor Robert E. Buswell Jr., held a postdoctoral fellowship at Washington University in St. Louis, and was at Dongguk University (attested 2012).

Richard F. Nance earned his PhD from the University of Chicago in 2004. Working in Buddhist studies, Indology, and religious studies, he was appointed Assistant Professor of South Asian Buddhism at Indiana University (attested 2013).
Richard Fick (1867–1944) was an Indologist who studied at the University of Kiel (~1886–1888). He later held a post at the University of Göttingen (~1921–1932).

Richard Foltz (b. 1961) studied at the University of Utah and Harvard University. Specializing in Iranian and Central Asian studies, religious studies, and history, he held posts at the University of Florida (~2003–2007) and Concordia University (~2007).
Richard Fritzsche (b. 1851) was an Indologist who studied under Hermann Brockhaus (~1873–1877). He later served as Rektor at Gymnasium Schneeberg.
